{{Short description|Italian mathematician (born c.1981)}}

'''Valentino Tosatti''' (born {{Circa|1981}}) is an Italian mathematician.

== Biography ==
Born {{Circa|1981}}, in [[Trieste]], Tosatti studied from 2000 at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]] and at the [[University of Pisa]], graduating with a ''[[laurea]]'' in 2004. He then studied at [[Harvard University]], where he graduated with an M.A. in 2005 and a Ph.D. in 2009.<ref name="CV">{{cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae: Valentino Tosatti|website=Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York University|url=https://cims.nyu.edu/~vt2234/cv.pdf}} (CV has comprehensive publication list.)</ref> His Ph.D. thesis ''Geometry of complex Monge-Ampère equations'' was supervised by [[Shing-Tung Yau]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=136698|name=Valentino Tosatti}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Tosatti, V.|title=Geometry of Complex Monge-Ampère Equations|year=2009|url=https://cims.nyu.edu/~vt2234/ma.pdf}}</ref> Tosatti was from 2009 to 2012 a Joseph Fels Ritt Assistant Professor at [[Columbia University]]. At [[Northwestern University]], he was an associate professor from 2012 to 2015 and a full professor from 2015 to 2020. From 2020 to 2022, he taught as a professor at [[McGill University]]. In 2022 he became a professor at [[New York University|NYU]]'s [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]].<ref name="CV" />

Tosatti does research on complex and differential geometry; geometric analysis on complex, Hermitian, and symplectic manifolds; and partial differential equations. He is also interested in the connections of his main research topics with algebraic geometry and dynamical systems.<ref name="CV" />

In 2017, with [[Gábor Székelyhidi]] and Ben Weinkove, Valentino Tosatti proved a conjecture published in 1984 by [[Paul Gauduchon]].<ref name=ActaMathematica>{{cite journal|arxiv=1503.04491 |doi=10.4310/ACTA.2017.v219.n1.a6  |doi-access=free|title=Gauduchon metrics with prescribed volume form |date=2017 |last1=Székelyhidi |first1=Gábor |last2=Tosatti |first2=Valentino |last3=Weinkove |first3=Ben |journal=Acta Mathematica |volume=219 |pages=181–211 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Gauduchon, Paul|title=La 1-forme de torsion d'une variété hermitienne compacte|journal=Mathematische Annalen|volume=267|year=1984|issue=4 |pages=495–518|doi=10.1007/BF01455968}}</ref> ''[[Acta Mathematica]]'' published their proof that on n-dimensional [[compact space|compact]] [[complex manifold]]s there is always a Gauduchon metric with prescribed [[volume form]]. For this purpose, the behavior of a large class of [[Elliptic differential equation|elliptic nonlinear partial differential equations]] of second order on [[Hermitian manifold]]s had to be investigated.<ref name=ActaMathematica/>

In 2011, Tosatti received a [[Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|Blavatnik Award]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Valentino Tosatti|website=Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists (blavatnikawards.org)|url=http://blavatnikawards.org/honorees/profile/valentino-tosatti/}}</ref> In 2012, he was awarded a two-year Sloan Research Fellowship.<ref name=CV/> In 2018, he received the [[Caccioppoli Prize]]. In 2019, he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for "contributions in geometric analysis and complex geometry".<ref>{{cite journal|title=2019 Class of Fellows of the AMS|date=March 2019|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=66|issue=3|pages=433–436|url=https://www.math.uh.edu/~minru/fellow19.pdf}}</ref>
